t:
(a) Definitions Relating to Motor Carriers.—Paragraphs (6), (7), (12), and (13) of section 13102 of title 49, United States Code, are each amended by striking “motor vehicle” and inserting “commercial motor vehicle (as defined in section 31132)”. 
    (b) Freight Forwarders.—Section 13903(a) of such title is amended—
        (1) by striking “The Secretary” and inserting the following:“(1) Household goods.—The Secretary”; 
        (2) by inserting “of household goods” after “freight forwarder”; and 
        (3) by adding at the end the following:“(2) Others.—The Secretary may register a person to provide service subject to jurisdiction under subchapter III of chapter 135 as a freight forwarder (other than a freight forwarder of household goods) if the Secretary finds that such registration is needed for the protection of shippers and that the person is fit, willing, and able to provide the service and to comply with this part and applicable regulations of the Secretary and Board.”.  
    (c) Brokers.—Section 13904(a) of such title is amended—
        (1) by striking “The Secretary” and inserting the following: “(1) Household Goods.—The Secretary”; 
        (2) by inserting “of household goods” after “broker”; and 
        (3) by adding at the end the following:“(2) Others.—The Secretary may register a person to provide service subject to jurisdiction under subchapter III of chapter 135 as a broker (other than a broker of household goods) if the Secretary finds that such registration is needed for the protection of shippers and that the person is fit, willing, and able to provide the service and to comply with this part and applicable regulations of the Secretary and Board.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to "applicable regulations of the Secretary and Board" or the registration process brings outside parties into a federal decision. But the section only amends definitions and lets the Secretary register freight forwarders and brokers, which is a license-type application rather than participation. The mention of regulations is a compliance condition referring to existing rules, not a grant of rulemaking authority, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary may register a person to provide service subject to jurisdiction under subchapter III of chapter 135 as a freight forwarder (other than a freight forwarder of household goods) if the Secretary finds that such registration is needed for the protection of shippers

opus.w: The section changes a definition and lets the Secretary register freight forwarders and brokers. Registration works like a license application, which the definition excludes. The mention of "applicable regulations" only points to rules that already exist. It does not grant or require new rulemaking, so the Example 6 rule about regulatory authority doesn't apply. No comment period, hearing, outside consultation, advisory body, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: The Secretary may register a person to provide service subject to jurisdiction under subchapter III of chapter 135 as a freight forwarder (other than a freight forwarder of household goods) if the Secretary finds that such registration is needed for the protection of shippers and that the person is fit, willing, and able to provide the service and to comply with this part and applicable regulations of the Secretary and Board.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The phrase "applicable regulations of the Secretary and Board" could look like rulemaking, which would count as participation. It isn't. The text only requires registrants to follow regulations that already exist. It doesn't give the Secretary any new power to make rules. The rest of the section is about registering freight forwarders and brokers, which is like a licensing application, and the definition excludes that.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the criteria for the Secretary to register freight forwarders and brokers. This is an administrative licensing or registration process. The definition explicitly states that 'applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses' are not participation. There is no requirement for the Secretary to consult with the public, states, or other outside entities before making the registration decision; the decision is based on the Secretary's findings regarding the applicant's fitness and the need for protection of shippers.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary may register a person to provide service subject to jurisdiction under subchapter III of chapter 135 as a freight forwarder (other than a freight forwarder of household goods) if the Secretary finds that such registration is needed for the protection of shippers and that the person is fit, willing, and able to provide the service and to comply with this part and applicable regulations of the Secretary and Board.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "protection of shippers" and "comply with... regulations of the Secretary and Board," implying some interaction with outside parties.
Resolution: This section describes the criteria for the Secretary to register freight forwarders and brokers. It is an administrative licensing/registration process, not a participatory decision-making process involving consultation with the public or outside entities before a policy decision. The "Board" mentioned is likely the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration or similar federal entity, or refers to existing regulations, but the act of registration itself is not participation as defined (consultation/coordination with outsiders before a decision). The definition explicitly excludes applications for licenses.
